title: Pauper's Ladder - The Brighthelm Chronicle Expansion (Review)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_O0v_5almw

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to one of his favourite games of all time, Pauper's Ladder, to show off what he calls one of the neatest expansions he has ever seen: the Brighthelm Chronicle, an "ultimate field guide" to the island. After a quick refresher on the base game — a lowly pauper roaming mines, swamps, forests and cities, chasing three of five virtues through quests, trophies and generosity — he makes the case for its real strength: a vivid sense of time and place, the thing he says separates a good game from a great one.

The striking part is that the Chronicle adds no rules at all. It is a book with an entry for nearly every encounter, item, bird, monster and pauper across the base game and its expansions, each with a short piece of lore and a few achievement checkboxes. He draws cards live and looks them up: Chessington, the mountain town built high to stay above its enemies (and now troubled only by giant eagles and dragons); the mysterious Seer Stones; and Sarah Bracken, the brewer who fell from grace after a fatal frenzy tasting.

Paul Stapleton's art is praised throughout. Daniel argues that the Chronicle changes his experience rather than the game, and he wishes Talisman or Runebound's Terrinoth had a companion atlas like it.

----

Would a lore-only expansion like the Brighthelm Chronicle make you play a favourite game more, and which game's world would you most want a companion atlas for?
